claims.text: Honest concession, not an argument: the record meets POL-NS-23. The driver sent in-app messages at 06:59:30 and 07:03:10 and placed an in-app call at 07:01:50, each before the 07:05:40 cancellation, and the trip record's own derived contact_before_cancel reports message_count 2, call_count 1, complete true and obligation_met true. The rider does not claim the driver failed to message or call, and the rider's case does not rest on that clause.

The fee rests on a deadline this record cannot fix. POL-NS-24 measures the rider's protection from 'the scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes'; this trip is on-demand, scheduled_at is null, and the trip record's own derived driver_deadline carries no deadline, giving the reason 'on-demand trip: no scheduled time'. The fact POL-NS-24 needs therefore cannot be established from this record, and POL-NS-24's own note directs POL-GEN-26 to apply where the deadline cannot be fixed. Under POL-GEN-26 the case goes to a human reviewer and, per POL-GEN-03, the 5.00 SGD is held rather than kept; that matters here because the ledger shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00 and a 5.00 cancellation fee line, so the rider is presently carrying the whole contested sum.

The objection that 'the AI ruling on a no-show is final' does not close the door. POL-NS-26 makes that finality expressly subject to POL-GEN-26, so where the deadline a no-show rule needs cannot be fixed, escalation is available in this category too and the otherwise-final AI ruling is displaced.

No profile history may decide this trip. POL-GEN-01 makes every rider- or driver-profile field context only, save the two fields it names and only for the tests that name them; the only rider-side counter any no-show clause names, rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d under POL-NS-25, is absent from this snapshot, so no repeat-no-show flag arises and the rider's history may not be used to convert an unfixed deadline into a rider loss.

The absence of a rider track is not evidence against the rider. The trace carries no rider track, so the record says nothing about where the rider was or when the rider was ready; POL-GEN-26 forbids inferring an outcome from absent evidence, and no no-show clause makes the rider's own location a condition of the driver's fee, so that gap cannot be read against the rider.

claims.text: The driver gave the rider the whole free wait he was entitled to. This was an on-demand booking with no scheduled pickup time, so under POL-NS-21 the 300-second free wait ran from the driver's arrival at 06:59:05 and expired at 07:04:05; the driver did not cancel until 07:05:40, 395 seconds after arrival and 95 seconds past expiry, so the no-show precondition for the fee is satisfied and the rider's lateness ('a few minutes late') is precisely the overrun the free wait is designed to absorb.

The arrival event is corroborated by the driver-device trace, which the pre-pass graded COMPLETE at weight 1.0 with no issue codes: the nearest fix in the 120-second window sits 6.57 m from the pickup point at 07:00:40 and reports an accuracy of 6 m, inside both the 25 m accuracy filter and the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, so POL-NS-21's arrival test is met and the arrival cannot be dismissed as a telemetry artefact.

The rider's only route to a refund runs through POL-NS-23, and it fails on the record. The driver sent an in-app message at 06:59:30 and a second at 07:03:10, and placed an in-app call at 07:01:50 that rang unanswered for 30 seconds - all three contacts before the 07:05:40 cancellation. Both limbs of the contact obligation (at least one in-app chat message AND at least one in-app call before cancellation) were therefore met, and the fee cannot be voided on this ground.

POL-NS-24 does not assist the rider either. It turns on a 'scheduled pickup time plus five minutes' deadline, and this was an on-demand booking whose scheduled_at is null, so no such deadline can be fixed on this record; the driver in any event arrived at 06:59:05 and attempted contact by message and call, so neither the full refund nor the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit that POL-NS-24 provides for a driver who failed to attempt contact is engaged.

The fare ledger shows exactly one 5.00 SGD cancellation-fee line, total_charged of 5.00 SGD, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, which matches the fee POL-NS-22 fixes for a no-show cancellation. Where the fee stands, POL-NS-22 makes the ruling DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both equal to the fee, and the fee share to the driver is the full 1.00, so the 5.00 SGD must be confirmed to the driver rather than returned to the rider.

The rider's own account concedes the material fact: 'I was only a few minutes late, my son was not ready' is an admission that the rider was not at the pickup point while the driver waited. The chat log bears this out - the driver's 06:59:30 message was read at 07:00:08 and the 07:03:10 message at 07:03:58, yet no reply was sent and the 07:01:50 call went unanswered - and nothing in the record shows the rider appearing within the 300-second free wait.

There is no basis to send this to a human. Neither profile carries a fraud flag (rider 0, driver 0) and the amount contested is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the confidence bar POL-GEN-22 imposes is the ordinary one and POL-NS-26 makes the AI ruling on this no-show final with the fee fixed at 5.00 SGD.

The traffic-advisory artifact for this trip is MISSING and carries weight 0.0 (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT); it is impaired evidence and supplies no fact about this trip. Its absence nonetheless leaves the driver's case untouched: POL-NS-21 runs the free wait from the driver's arrival on an on-demand trip and does not turn on traffic conditions, so there is no missing traffic record capable of excusing the rider's failure to appear during the wait.

I reject the rider's argument that POL-NS-24 read with POL-GEN-26 forces escalation. POL-NS-24 is the driver-no-show protection: it applies where the driver fails to arrive by the scheduled pickup time plus five minutes. ruling.explanation:
Both sides agree on what the record shows, and the record decides this case.

TRIP AND FREE WAIT (POL-NS-21). TRP-06051 was an on-demand RydeX booking (Block 77, Commonwealth Drive, booked 06:52:20, scheduled_at null), so there was no scheduled pickup time and the 300-second free wait ran from the driver's arrival. The driver arrived at 06:59:05 — the auto-arrival is corroborated by the driver-device trace EV-GPS-06051, whose nearest fix sits 6.57 m from the pickup at 06:59:40 with 6 m reported accuracy, inside the 25 m accuracy filter and the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius — the wait expired at 07:04:05, and the driver cancelled at 07:05:40, 395 seconds after arrival and 95 seconds past expiry. The no-show precondition is met, and the rider's own account ('I was only a few minutes late, my son was not ready') is precisely the overrun the free wait exists to absorb.

CONTACT (POL-NS-23). Before cancelling at 07:05:40 the driver sent in-app messages at 06:59:30 and 07:03:10 and placed an in-app call at 07:01:50 that rang unanswered (EV-CHAT-06051, EV-TRIP-06051; the trip record's own contact_before_cancel reports message_count 2, call_count 1, obligation_met true). Both limbs of the contact obligation are met, so the fee is not voided on this ground. Both advocates concede this.

THE FEE (POL-NS-22). EV-FARE-06051 shows a single 5.00 SGD cancellation-fee line, total charged 5.00 SGD, payment status CHARGED and refund issued 0.00 — exactly the 5.00 SGD POL-NS-22 fixes for a no-show. Where the fee stands, POL-NS-22 directs DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both equal to the fee charged. That is 5.00 SGD and 5.00 SGD.

THE RIDER'S POINTS, ANSWERED. (1) POL-NS-24 is the 'driver was late' remedy and does not apply: the driver did arrive at 06:59:05 and did attempt contact by message and call, so neither POL-NS-24's full refund nor its 5.00 SGD goodwill credit (which is for a driver who also failed to attempt contact) is engaged. (2) The rider's escalation argument under POL-GEN-26 fails. POL-GEN-26 escalates only where a fact the case needs cannot be established because the evidence carrying it is missing or impaired, and every artifact that carries a deciding fact — the trip record, the GPS trace, the chat log and the fare ledger — is COMPLETE at weight 1.0. The reference time the no-show fee needs is supplied by POL-NS-21 itself. (3) The absent rider track (EV-GPS-06051) proves nothing either way: no clause makes the rider's own location a test, and POL-GEN-26 forbids reading an absence against a party — so it cannot help the rider's refund any more than it can hurt. (4) The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-06051-01 (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) carries no fact and POL-NS-21 does not turn on traffic, so its absence changes nothing.

PROFILES AND WHO DECIDES. POL-GEN-01 makes party history context only, and neither profile decides this trip. Neither profile carries a fraud flag (rider 0, driver 0) and the contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so under POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26 the AI ruling is final. POL-NS-25 does not fire: the rider profile does not carry no_show_cancellations_30d, so no repeat-no-show flag arises.

One open point for the file, not a referral: because this was an on-demand trip, the trip record carries no scheduled pickup time and its derived driver_deadline is null. That does not block the fee, whose conditions are fixed by POL-NS-21 and met, but it is why the driver-lateness limb of POL-NS-24 cannot be measured and is left unapplied.

No referral arises. POL-NS-24's goodwill credit is not engaged (contact was attempted), the fee is exactly 5.00 SGD so POL-NS-22's fee-amount check is not triggered, and POL-NS-25's counter is absent. THE OUTCOME: the 5.00 SGD no-show fee stands and is confirmed to the driver as compensation; the rider's request for a refund is not supported.
